eventExtraction.categoryIntro: Extract all clinically relevant and actionable events in the following categories:

categories.name: Genetic variants
categories.block:
**Category 1 — Genetic variants (ALWAYS include the gene and variant type):**
Do NOT output a bare gene name. ALWAYS append the variant type.
Examples: "MYBPC3 mutation", "KCNQ1 mutation", "LMNA mutation", "TTN truncating variant"

categories.name: Functional / imaging findings
categories.block:
**Category 2 — Functional / imaging findings:**
"LVEF 25%", "septal hypertrophy", "late gadolinium enhancement", "LVOT gradient 60 mmHg"

categories.name: Arrhythmia / electrophysiology findings
categories.block:
**Category 3 — Arrhythmia / electrophysiology findings:**
"QTc prolongation", "non-sustained ventricular tachycardia", "atrial fibrillation"

postCategoryNotes: Focus on information that is directly relevant to potential therapy selection or clinical management. Avoid vague or redundant information like "stable vital signs".

CRITICAL: For genetic events, NEVER emit just a gene name (e.g., "MYBPC3"). ALWAYS include the variant type (e.g., "MYBPC3 mutation"). A bare gene name is not an actionable event — the variant type determines whether it is clinically significant.

fewShotExample.caseNoteInput: 45-year-old man presents with exertional dyspnea and a family history of sudden cardiac death. Echocardiogram shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy with LVOT gradient of 60 mmHg. Genetic testing reveals a pathogenic MYBPC3 mutation. Holter monitor shows non-sustained ventricular tachycardia.
fewShotExample.expectedOutput: "MYBPC3 mutation" "septal hypertrophy" "LVOT gradient 60 mmHg" "non-sustained ventricular tachycardia"

guidanceNotes: **Focus on Actionable Events:** We are not trying to summarize the case but to find what information is relevant to decision-making. This helps filter noise and focus on clinically significant findings.
**Prioritization:** Prioritizing genotype-driven studies ensures searches are matched to the patient's specific inherited or structural cardiac condition.
**Specific Search Terms:** Using exact terms such as "MYBPC3 mutation" is essential for precision. Adding "therapy", "treatment" or "clinical trials" helps to find relevant studies.
**Combinations:** Combining genetic and functional/imaging features allows for refined searches that might be more relevant to the patient.
**Iteration:** If initial search results are not helpful, we can modify and refine the queries based on the available data.

articleScoring.evaluationGoal: evaluate full research articles related to cardiovascular disease, especially those concerning inherited cardiac conditions, to identify potential advancements in treatment and understanding of the disease

domainFilterField.label: Cardiac Focus
domainFilterField.description: Whether the article relates to cardiovascular disease

fields.label: Disease Match
fields.description: Set to true if the article's disease focus matches the patient's disease. Articles that cover the exact condition in question receive significant points.

fields.label: Drugs Tested
fields.description: Whether any drugs or interventions are mentioned as tested

fields.label: Treatment Results
fields.description: Set to true if the article demonstrates positive treatment results

fields.label: Cell Studies
fields.description: Whether interventions were tested on cells in vitro (e.g. iPSC-cardiomyocytes)

fields.label: Animal Model Studies
fields.description: Whether interventions were tested in animal models

fields.label: Case Report
fields.description: Whether the article presents a case report

fields.label: Series of Case Reports
fields.description: Whether the article presents multiple case reports

fields.label: Clinical Study
fields.description: Whether the article describes a clinical study

fields.label: Novelty
fields.description: If the paper describes a novel mechanism or therapeutic strategy
